statement: Under the standing cofibration and colimit hypotheses, let $u:I\to I^{\prime}$ be a map of artinian posets; assume either both associated spaces are noetherian, or transfinite composites of cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are allowed. If $u^*$ carries cofibrant diagrams to cofibrant diagrams, the functor induced by $u_!$ on cofibrant diagrams is left adjoint to localized restriction $u_W^*$.
notes: The beginning of the statement is on the unmarked tail of manuscript p.57; p.58 begins at alternative (b). Colimit existence is inherited from the preceding construction, as made explicit in Theorem 3.7.

statement: The preservation hypothesis of Corollary 3.5 holds when every comma poset $(i^{\prime}\downarrow u)$ is locally cofiltered.
notes: Here locally cofiltered means each connected component is cofiltered; this is a condition for restriction on cofibrant diagrams, not the comma category in the pointwise left-Kan formula.

statement: Let $F\dashv G$ between relative categories, with $G$ homotopical. If a full subcategory $\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C$ induces an equivalence after localization and $F|_{\mathcal C_0}$ is homotopical, one obtains a functor $\overline F=\operatorname{Ho}(F|_{\mathcal C_0})\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal C_0\hookrightarrow\mathcal C)^{-1}$, defined up to canonical isomorphism, and $\overline G=\operatorname{Ho}(G)$.
notes: The existence of a quasi-inverse is used; canonical uniqueness is up to the appropriate natural isomorphism.

statement: The hypotheses of Remark 3.6 do not imply $\overline F\dashv\overline G$.
repair: The walking-arrow example in the commentary makes the counterexample explicit. A sufficient replacement is an actual left deformation, or absolute derived functors on both sides.
references: Grothendieck1990XVII, Remark 3.6; Riehl2014, Theorems 2.2.8 and 2.2.11; Maltsiniotis2007Adjunction, unnumbered theorem

statement: For $\mathcal C=\mathcal C^{\prime}$, $F=G=1$, $W=\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal C$, $W^{\prime}=\operatorname{Iso}\mathcal C$, the induced right functor is $\mathcal C\to\Pi\mathcal C$. If $\Pi\mathcal C\simeq 1$ and $e$ has only its identity endomorphism, the selected subcategory $\{e\}$ induces a localization equivalence; its selected left functor is adjoint precisely when $e$ is initial.
notes: The source calls this 1-connectedness. It is a statement about the groupoid completion, not contractibility in all homotopy degrees.

statement: A terminal object $e$ has trivial endomorphism group and makes $\Pi\mathcal C$ equivalent to the terminal groupoid; it need not be initial.
notes: The category $0\to1$ with $e=1$ already suffices.

statement: For a category with cofibrations admitting finite colimits and $u:I\to I^{\prime}$ between artinian posets, the cofibrant-diagram construction $u_!^W$ is left adjoint to $u_W^*$ if either the associated spaces are noetherian, or $C$ and $C\cap W$ are closed under transfinite composition and $\mathcal M$ admits small filtered colimits.
notes: The proof factors the indexing functor, not the coefficient object. The colimit hypothesis in alternative (b) is material.

statement: The categorical mapping cylinder $C(u)$ has objects $\operatorname{Ob}I\sqcup\operatorname{Ob}I^{\prime}$, original arrows within each summand, no arrows from $I$ to $I^{\prime}$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{C(u)}(j,i)=\operatorname{Hom}_{I^{\prime}}(j,u i)$. It factors $u=v w$, with $w$ the cosieve inclusion and $v$ the canonical retraction.
notes: The text calls this a mapping-cone; the displayed categorical pushout is a mapping cylinder/collage.

statement: For each $j\in I^{\prime}$, the comma category $(j\downarrow v)$ is the collage of $(j\downarrow I^{\prime})$ and $(j\downarrow u)$, with mixed arrows the commutative triangles under $j$.
For every small-category functor $u$, the category $(j\downarrow v)$ has initial object $(j,1_j)$; consequently $v$ satisfies the local cofilteredness condition needed in Corollary 3.5.
notes: An initial object makes the comma category cofiltered: a common predecessor and equalizing predecessor are supplied by that object. The result is valid beyond posets.

statement: If $I,I^{\prime}$ are artinian posets, then so is $C(u)$; noetherianity of their associated spaces also passes to $C(u)$.
repair: An alternating chain can cross the two summands at most once. An increasing chain of open subsets stabilizes after its intersections with both summands stabilize.

statement: For the cosieve $w:I\hookrightarrow C(u)$, covariant left Kan extension is extension by the initial object outside $I$ and agrees with the diagram on $I$. Both $w_!$ and $w^*$ preserve pointwise weak equivalences, so their ordinary adjunction descends.
gap_or_error: The target of $w_!$ is mislabelled in the printed line: the text says $I=C(u)$ and then uses $J$ for the target.
repair: Read $J=C(u)$ throughout that calculation. The mathematical proof is unchanged.

statement: The derived left Kan extension for $u=v w$ identifies with $v_!^W w_!^W$, and localized restriction with $w_W^*v_W^*$; composing the two adjunctions proves Theorem 3.7.
notes: Compatibility of the cofibrant constructions with composition is a previously established input; this is not a general theorem that arbitrary derived functors compose.

statement: On the indicated domain of artinian posets, the prederivator $\mathbf D_W$ satisfies the source axioms Dér 1 (decomposition), Dér 2 (localization), Dér 3 (terminal object), Dér 4 bis (left adjoints to restriction), Dér 5 bis (pointwise computation), and the cocartesian half of Dér 6.
gap_or_error: The transfinite derivator conclusion switches from covariant diagrams $\mathcal M(I^\circ)$ to the presheaf prederivator $\mathbf D_W(I)$ without reversing the class of admissible posets. The preceding colimit hypotheses also remain standing.
repair: For $\mathbf D_W(I)=\operatorname{Ho}\mathcal M(I)$ use noetherian $I$, with $\operatorname{Esp}(I^\circ)$ noetherian in the finite-domain alternative. This reindexing is explicit in Chapter XIX, 3.2–3.4. Keep the original axiom numbers distinct from present conventions.

statement: The decomposition assertion in Corollary 3.9 says that localization of diagrams over an admissible disjoint union splits as the product of the corresponding localized diagram categories, with the empty diagram category terminal.
notes: This is the content of the cited Dér 1; the available disjoint unions are restricted by the chosen diagram domain.

statement: The localization assertion in Corollary 3.9 includes joint conservativity of evaluation: a morphism in the localized diagram category is invertible if its values at every object are invertible.
notes: The source cites earlier localization work; this is not true for arbitrary relative categories from two-out-of-three alone.

statement: The terminal-object axiom cited as Dér 3 asserts full faithfulness of the constant-diagram functor $p^*: \mathbf D(e)\to\mathbf D(S)$ when the admissible indexing category $S$ has a final object.
references: Grothendieck1990XVII, Corollary 3.9; Grothendieck1990XIX, proof of Corollary 2.4, manuscript pp.23–24
notes: This is not an assertion that the category $\mathbf D(e)$ has a terminal object. In an adjunction $p_!\dashv p^*$ it says that the counit $p_!p^*\to1$ is invertible.

statement: The cited Dér 4 bis asserts a left adjoint $u_!$ for restriction along every map in the corrected diagram domain.
notes: These three assertions retain Grothendieck's numbering. The square class is the relative $W$-cocartesian class used in the preceding chapters.

statement: Theorem 3.7, formulated for covariant diagrams on artinian posets, immediately proves the corresponding restriction of the presheaf prederivator on the same artinian posets.
gap_or_error: This inference omits the opposite in the indexing category. It does not establish the stated presheaf-domain assertion from that theorem.
repair: Reindex by $I^{\mathrm{op}}$: presheaf diagrams are controlled on noetherian posets, with the associated opposite-poset topology in the noetherian-topology clause. Grothendieck makes this correction explicitly in Chapter XIX, 3.2–3.4.
notes: The inference is false as written; no claim is made that a later arbitrary-shape theorem fails on artinian shapes.

statement: The cited Dér 5 bis identifies evaluations of left homotopy Kan extensions with homotopy colimits over the appropriate comma categories, with opposites inserted for presheaf diagrams.
notes: Keep the source axiom numbering distinct from modern Der4 notation.

statement: The cocartesian part of the cited Dér 6 asserts invertibility of the left-Kan base-change mate on the source class of $W$-cocartesian squares.
notes: The square class is the relative $W$-cocartesian class used in the preceding chapters.

statement: To add the right Kan extensions, their pointwise formula, and cartesian exactness, one may supply a dual fibration-category structure with the same weak equivalences; cross-lifting relations between the chosen cofibrations and fibrations are not required for this two-sided derivator strategy.
notes: This is a programme at this point. The later ABC theorem has its own completeness and cocompleteness axioms.

statement: A Quillen structure additionally imposes the two lifting/factorization pairs $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$; the one-sided Brown-type axioms do not impose these cross-relations.
notes: No assertion that every independent pair of Brown structures is a Quillen structure is made.

statement: For arbitrary target category $I^{\prime}$ and artinian-poset source $I$, the displayed formula $(u_!X)(j)=\operatorname{colim}_{(u\downarrow j)}X$ still constructs a weak-equivalence-preserving functor on cofibrant diagrams without further hypotheses.
gap_or_error: As an extension of the finite-colimit alternative, this omits existence and admissibility of the larger comma-indexed colimits. The comma category may have infinitely many objects above a single source object.
repair: Use the transfinite alternative with all required small colimits and stability, or explicitly require every relevant comma category and colimit to lie in the range of the earlier theorem. For $\mathcal M=\mathrm{FinSet}$, $C=$ all maps and $W=$ isomorphisms, $e\to B\mathbb Z$ has no ordinary left adjoint to restriction; the commentary gives a finite-orbit proof.
notes: The pointwise formula itself is correct when its colimits exist; no defect is asserted under the transfinite hypotheses.

statement: The projection $(u\downarrow j)\to I$ is a discrete fibration; when $I$ is a poset the comma category is again a poset, and restriction preserves the local cofibration conditions used earlier.
gap_or_error: Artinianity passes to this comma poset, but noetherianity need not pass when fibres are infinite.
repair: Retain the necessary size/colimit hypothesis; do not infer topological noetherianity from the word étale.

statement: Without a suitable cofibration structure on diagrams over non-posets, the mapping-cylinder proof of Theorem 3.7 has not yet established the adjunction for arbitrary target shapes.
repair: The current section constructs projective cofibration structures under special hypotheses. Later ABC theory proves arbitrary-shape adjunctions under its complete axioms.
notes: Open records the author's position here, not an assertion that this question remains open today.

statement: Full faithfulness of a functor of underlying categories does not by itself imply full faithfulness after localization, even when the resulting functor is a right adjoint.
notes: Take $\mathcal C=[1]$, source weak equivalences the isomorphisms, target weak equivalences all arrows. The localization $[1]\to1$ has left adjoint selecting 0 but is not fully faithful.

statement: The inference attributed here to Anderson, from ordinary full faithfulness of restriction to full faithfulness of localized restriction without further control of derived unit/counit, is not a valid formal implication.
repair: The counterexample just given disproves the formal implication. This audit does not independently identify the precise passage of Anderson's paper criticized by Grothendieck.
notes: The conclusion for particular homotopically cofinal functors may still be true; the failed inference does not refute those conclusions.

statement: A strict category with cofibrations is one for which cofibration–weak-equivalence factorizations can be chosen naturally on every small diagram of arrows; globally functorial factorization implies this property.
notes: The arrow-category qualification handles large categories; it is not an assertion of a small globally chosen functor without universe conventions.

statement: For an essentially small category, existence of pointwise cofibration–weak-equivalence factorizations in every small diagram category is equivalent to functorial factorization, by applying it to the universal diagram indexed by the arrow category.
notes: Pass to a small equivalent category before using its arrow category as an index.

statement: If the cofibration category is strict, passing to coefficients $\mathcal M^Z$ gives the same relative left-derivator assertions for arbitrary small parameter $Z$ and the stated admissible maps; the source repeats the artinian indexing convention at this step.
gap_or_error: The presheaf convention in $\mathbf D_Z$ requires the opposite class of posets from that used for covariant diagrams in Theorem 3.7.
repair: Use the noetherian domain and, where relevant, noetherianity of $\operatorname{Esp}(I^\circ)$; alternatively state the result throughout for the covariant-diagram convention. Chapter XIX, 3.2–3.4 supplies the explicit corrected presheaf formulation.
notes: Objectwise colimits and closure conditions pass to $\mathcal M^Z$; strictness supplies the objectwise factorization axiom.

statement: For the presheaf convention $\mathbf D_W(I)=\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M^{I^{\mathrm{op}}})$, the square with upper-right corner $(i^{\prime}\downarrow u)\times Z$ gives the pointwise left-Kan formula, using the canonical comma 2-cell and the opposite of the comma category as colimit index.
repair: The printed comma symbol is correct after the return to the presheaf convention in 3.11. The admissible class of posets must instead be reindexed by opposites as explained in Chapter XIX, 3.2–3.4.
notes: An initial suspicion of a comma-variance error was rejected after checking the coefficient convention; no comma-symbol correction is applied.

statement: Find hypotheses on a strict cofibration category guaranteeing all small left homotopy Kan extensions and their pointwise formula.
repair: Special cofibration categories are the present proposed route; ABC cofibration categories give a later affirmative answer via simplicial resolutions, without requiring special/cofibrantly generated structure.

statement: Assume the relevant small colimits, smallness of objects, the pushout/composition axioms for $C$ and $TC=C\cap W$, closure of both classes under transfinite composition, and a set $C_0\subset C$ with $C\subset\widetilde{C_0}$. Then every map factors as $pi$ with $i\in C$ and $p\in C_*$.
repair: Choose a regular cardinal uniformly large for the domains of the set $C_0$ and run the small-object argument; its left factor is a relative $C_0$-cell map and hence lies in $C$.
notes: $\widetilde S={}^\perp(S^\perp)$ is Quillen left closure; the tilde is not closure under weak equivalence.

statement: $TF:=C_*$ is the class of maps with the right lifting property against every map of $C$.
For $C_0\subset C$, the condition $C\subset\widetilde{C_0}$ is equivalent to $C_*=(C_0)_*$.
notes: This is the Galois correspondence of lifting classes, independent of the small-object argument.

statement: Under the preceding small-object hypotheses, $C_*\subset W$ implies the cofibration–weak-equivalence factorization axiom.
If the cofibration structure comes from a closed Quillen structure $(W,C,F)$, both $C$ and $TC=C\cap W$ are closed under the relevant transfinite compositions.
repair: Each class is a left lifting class, respectively against $F\cap W$ and $F$; fillers through a transfinite composite are constructed by induction and the colimit universal property.

statement: Conversely, the cofibration–weak-equivalence factorization axiom implies $C_*\subset W$ if $W$ is retract-closed.
repair: Factor $p\in C_*$ as $p=q i$ with $i\in C,q\in W$. A lift against $i$ makes $p$ a retract of $q$ in the arrow category.
notes: Retract closure is a genuine hypothesis here; it is not implied by bare two-out-of-three.

statement: Starting with a set $C_0$ such that $(C_0)_*\subset W$, let $C$ be either its pushout/transfinite closure or its Quillen closure. The closure and factorization axioms hold; the remaining substantive requirement is pushout closure of $C\cap W$.
The heuristic sentence says these conditions will practically only be met when $W$ is not closed under filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: The PDF has an extraneous negation, contradicted by the positive stability hypothesis explicitly used in the next paragraph.
repair: Read the intended heuristic with $W$ closed under filtered colimits. This is an interpretation of a textual slip, not a theorem asserting necessity.
notes: The printed wording remains in the reader.

statement: Under the stated small-object hypotheses, the Quillen closure of the generating set $C_0$ is the class of retracts of maps in its pushout/transfinite closure.
repair: Factor a map in the left lifting class by the small-object argument and apply its left lifting property against the right factor; it is a retract of the cellular factor.
notes: This is an identification using the small-object hypotheses, not the definition of Quillen closure in arbitrary categories.

statement: If $W$ is closed under small filtered colimits in the arrow category and $C_0\subset\operatorname{Cof}_W$, then either indicated closure $C$ also lies in $\operatorname{Cof}_W$.
repair: Pushout stability is formal; successive pushout functors preserve weak equivalences, and at limit stages use filtered-colimit stability of $W$. Retract closure of $W$ follows by expressing a retract as a sequential colimit.

statement: Filtered-colimit closure of a class $W$ of arrows implies retract closure.
repair: For a retract $f$ of $g\in W$, the sequential arrow-diagram $g\xrightarrow e g\xrightarrow e\cdots$ for the associated idempotent has colimit $f$. Its terms lie in $W$.
notes: This is closure under filtered colimits of diagrams of arrows, not merely closure under transfinite composites of arrows belonging to $W$.

statement: Under the enough-factorization hypothesis available in 4.2, intrinsic homotopy cofibrations satisfy $\operatorname{Cof}_W\cap W=W^{\mathrm{univ}}$, the weak equivalences preserved by every pushout. Consequently $TC=C\cap W^{\mathrm{univ}}$ is pushout-stable when $C\subset\operatorname{Cof}_W$.
repair: Factor an arbitrary base-change map as an intrinsic cofibration followed by a weak equivalence; the two pushout comparisons and two-out-of-three show universal pushout stability. The commentary gives the complete argument.
notes: The identity is an earlier input, not newly proved in this excerpt; the enough-factorization hypothesis is essential to the supplied verification.

statement: If $C$ is transfinite-composition closed and $W$ is closed under filtered colimits, then $TC=C\cap W$ is closed under transfinite composition.
notes: At successor stages use composition/identities in $W$; at limit stages apply filtered-colimit closure to the arrows from the first object.

statement: For a small category $I$, let $I_0$ be its discrete object set and $v_I:I_0\to I$ the identity-on-objects functor. Its restriction functor on diagrams has left adjoint $v_!$; this adjunction will transfer the objectwise structure on $\mathcal M^{I_0}$.
notes: These left Kan extensions exist under the cocompleteness hypothesis introduced in Section 4.

statement: A special cofibration structure has a locally small cocomplete coefficient category in which each object is small for some sufficiently filtered colimits, as required by the factorization theorem.
notes: The word accessible here is an objectwise smallness condition; the statement does not itself assert local presentability or a set of presentable generators.

statement: In a special cofibration structure, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, $C$ is closed under pushout and composition, and $TC=C\cap W$ is closed under pushout (hence also composition).
notes: The standing convention that the cofibration classes contain isomorphisms is retained.

statement: In a special cofibration structure, $C$ and $TC$ are closed under transfinite composition.
In a special cofibration structure there exists a set $C_0\subset C$ with $C\subset\widetilde{C_0}$, equivalently $\widetilde C=\widetilde{C_0}$.
In a special cofibration structure, $TF=C_*\subset W$; together with the preceding axioms this supplies the factorization axiom.
Given $L=v_!\dashv U=v^*$, define $W^{\prime}=U^{-1}(W)$ and $C^{\prime}$ as the closure of $L(C)$ under pushouts and transfinite composition.
$L(C)\subset C^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(C)}=\widetilde{C^{\prime}}$, and $W^{\prime}$ satisfies two-out-of-three.
The classes just defined will be special cofibration structures, with an optional retract completion of $C^{\prime}$.
gap_or_error: This is an announcement before all necessary hypotheses have been introduced, rather than a theorem under only the assumptions preceding (4.5.1).
repair: Read with the additional assumptions collected in Proposition 4.6; its retract-completed variant assumes $C=\widetilde C$.

statement: If $U$ preserves pushouts and carries $C^{\prime}$ into $C$, then $TC^{\prime}=C^{\prime}\cap W^{\prime}$ is pushout-stable.
gap_or_error: The printed last line on p.75 writes $U(j^{\prime})\in W^{\prime}$; its correct type is $U(j^{\prime})\in W$.
repair: Use $U(TC^{\prime})\subset C\cap W$ and pushout stability of $C\cap W$.

statement: If $U$ preserves all small colimits and $UL(C)\subset C$, then $U(C^{\prime})\subset C$ and $U(TC^{\prime})\subset TC$.
notes: The proof needs the relevant pushouts and ordinal colimits; all-small-colimit preservation is a convenient sufficient assumption.

statement: Under the preceding hypotheses and $C=\widetilde C$, one also has $U(\widetilde{C^{\prime}})\subset C$ and $U(\widetilde{C^{\prime}}\cap W^{\prime})\subset TC$.
notes: Every functor preserves retract diagrams. The small-object argument identifies the Quillen closure with retracts of the cellular class.

statement: Under these hypotheses $TC^{\prime}$ is transfinite-composition closed; the same holds for $\widetilde{C^{\prime}}\cap W^{\prime}$ when $C$ is retract-closed.
If $C_0$ is the small generating set for $C$, then $L(C_0)\subset C^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(C_0)}$, so the transferred class has a small generating set for its lifting closure.
notes: The left adjoint preserves colimits, and every functor preserves retracts.

statement: For $TF^{\prime}=(C^{\prime})_*$ one has $TF^{\prime}=(L C)_*=U^{-1}(C_*)=U^{-1}(TF)$, independently of taking the retract completion of $C^{\prime}$.
notes: This is the adjunction bijection between lifting problems, together with closure of left lifting classes under pushouts and transfinite composites.

statement: $TF\subset W$ implies $TF^{\prime}\subset W^{\prime}$.

Let $L\dashv U$ with special source, cocomplete target with small objects, $U$ colimit-preserving, and $UL(C)\subset C$. Then $(\mathcal M^{\prime},U^{-1}W,\operatorname{cell}(LC))$ is a special cofibration category.
notes: No generating set of trivial cofibrations is assumed; this establishes one-sided cofibration structure, not yet a complete Quillen model structure.

statement: If additionally $C=\widetilde C$, replacing the transferred cellular class by its retract closure still gives a special cofibration structure.
notes: Footnote 20 proposes an alternative using retract and transfinite stability of $W$, developed in Proposition 5.1; it is not an unconditional deletion of hypotheses.

statement: Under suitable additional assumptions, seek $L(TC)\subset TC^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(TC)}$, or the stronger $\widetilde{C^{\prime}}\cap W^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(TC)}$.
repair: The forward inclusion has the extra criterion (4.7.4); the converse closure comparison is treated later in Proposition 5.8 under its Quillen/factorization hypotheses.
notes: Source-stage question, not an assertion of present-day unresolved status.

statement: Under Proposition 4.6, $L(TC)\subset TC^{\prime}$ is equivalent to $UL(TC)\subset TC$.
notes: Since $L(TC)\subset C^{\prime}$ and $UL(TC)\subset C$, each condition reduces to preservation of weak equivalences on $TC$.

statement: Define $F=(TC)_*$, $F^{\prime}=(TC^{\prime})_*$ and $F^{\prime}_{\sim}=(\widetilde{C^{\prime}}\cap W^{\prime})_*$.
notes: These lifting classes are candidates for fibrations; the notation does not assert a Quillen structure.

statement: Assuming $L(TC)\subset TC^{\prime}$, one has $F^{\prime}_{\sim}\subset F^{\prime}\subset U^{-1}(F)$.

Under the same inclusion, $TC^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(TC)}$ is equivalent to $F^{\prime}=U^{-1}(F)$; similarly $\widetilde{C^{\prime}}\cap W^{\prime}\subset\widetilde{L(TC)}$ is equivalent to $F^{\prime}_{\sim}=U^{-1}(F)$.
notes: This equivalence uses Quillen/Galois left closure, not an unsupported equality with a cell closure.

statement: For a special cofibration structure, $(\widetilde C\cap W)^\perp=(C\cap W)^\perp$; hence the two target fibration candidates $F_{\sim}'$ and $F'$ coincide.
repair: Proposition 5.1 proves that each arrow of the enlarged trivial class is a retract of an arrow of the original trivial class; right lifting classes are unchanged by retract closure.
notes: No retract stability of W is needed for equality of the right lifting classes.

statement: Under what additional assumptions does $F'=(v^*)^{-1}(F)$ hold for the transferred cofibration structure?
repair: Resolved in the same chapter by Proposition 5.8 for a special closed coefficient Quillen triple and the stated transfer hypotheses.
notes: Open only at this point in the source, not asserted to remain open today.

statement: For a small discrete category $I_0$, the componentwise classes $W(I_0)$ and $C(I_0)$ make $\mathcal M^{I_0}$ a special cofibration category.
repair: A generating set consists of each coefficient generator in one coordinate with identity of the initial object elsewhere; the other axioms are componentwise.
references: Grothendieck1990XVII, manuscript pp.81--82; Hirschhorn2003, Proposition 11.1.10 (comparison: cofibrantly generated model-category case); Riehl2014, section 12.3
notes: This assertion precedes the displayed conclusion of Proposition 4.8.

statement: The category $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{op},\mathcal M)$ is cocomplete and each of its objects is accessible when the same holds in $\mathcal M$.
repair: Colimits are pointwise; choose a common regular smallness bound for the small set of components and naturality equations, then use the equalizer-of-products formula for natural transformations.
notes: The source says this follows immediately. The commentary supplies the cardinal-bound argument.

statement: The restriction $v^*:\mathcal M(I)\to\mathcal M(I_0)$ preserves all small colimits.
notes: Computed componentwise.

statement: The endofunctor $v^*v_!$ preserves componentwise cofibrations and componentwise trivial cofibrations on $\mathcal M(I_0)$.
gap_or_error: Equation (4.8.1) writes TC(I) in both positions, although the endofunctor acts on M(I_0).
repair: Read both classes as TC(I_0), as is done in the proof; use the explicit coproduct formula.
notes: Edition slip, retained in the source text; the correctly typed proposition is proved.

statement: Define $W(I)=(v^*)^{-1}W(I_0)$ and let $C(I)$ be the cobase-change and transfinite-composition closure of $v_!C(I_0)$. These form a special cofibration structure.
notes: Proposition 4.8; follows by the verified free-diagram hypotheses.

statement: $TF(I)=C(I)^\perp=(v^*)^{-1}TF(I_0)$, so trivial fibrations are componentwise.
repair: Transport lifting squares along v_! ⊣ v^*; taking cellular closure does not change right lifting classes.
notes: Equation (4.8.8).

statement: $v_!(TC(I_0))\subset TC(I)$.
repair: The free endofunctor preserves componentwise trivial cofibrations, so its left adjoint sends them into the prescribed weak equivalences and into C(I).
notes: First inclusion of (4.8.9).

statement: $F(I)=(TC(I))^\perp\subset(v^*)^{-1}F(I_0)$.
repair: Apply right orthogonality to the preceding inclusion and adjointness.
notes: Second inclusion of (4.8.9).

statement: Footnote 23 proposes the literal equality $v_!(TC(I_0))=TC(I)$ under stronger special-model hypotheses.
gap_or_error: The raw image of the free diagram functor need not be closed under pushout, even in a special closed model structure.
repair: Only equality after Q-closure is true. For Set with W=all, C=injections, F=surjections, and I=B(Z/2), the map *→*⊔(Z/2) is a transferred trivial cofibration but cannot be a free image, because its domain has a fixed point.
references: Grothendieck1990XVII, Theorem 6.1(b); this companion, block at ms.83, A free cell does not make every cofibration free
notes: The counterexample is proved completely in the commentary. It does not refute the fibration equality in the same footnote.

statement: Footnote 23 proposes $F(I)=(v^*)^{-1}F(I_0)$ under stronger special-model hypotheses.
repair: Proposition 5.8 proves this equality, and Theorem 6.1 applies it to diagram categories.
notes: Affirmative under the hypotheses subsequently stated; no unconditional claim added.

statement: For a family $X$, $(v_!X)(i)=\coprod_{j\in Ob I}\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)\cdot X_j$.
notes: The superscript notation in the edition denotes a coproduct of copies. It is not a cartesian power. Diagrams are contravariant.

statement: Any class of maps containing isomorphisms and stable under cobase change and continuous transfinite composition is stable under arbitrary small coproducts.
repair: Well-order the family and successively replace each source summand by its target. Each successor map is a pushout of one family member and the limit stages are coproduct colimits.
notes: Footnote 25 requests the general lemma; the commentary proves it, including the empty family.

statement: $TF=C^\perp$, $TC=C\cap W$, and $F=(TC)^\perp$.
notes: Equation (5.1); star below denotes right lifting class.

statement: $TC\subset C$, $TF\subset F$, $C\perp TF$, and $TC\perp F$; $(C,TF)$ has factorization and is closed on the right.
repair: The inclusions and lifting properties follow from the definitions; the factorization was obtained from specialness in section 4.
notes: Diagram (5.2). Closed on the right means TF=C^perp; it does not assert C is retract-closed.

statement: $\widetilde C={}^{\perp}(C^\perp)$ is the retract closure of $C$.
repair: Factor an arrow of the left lifting class as C followed by TF and use the lift to exhibit it as a retract of its left factor.
references: Grothendieck1990XVII, manuscript pp.84; Riehl2014, Lemma 11.2.3; Grothendieck1990XV, Proposition 4.2, Corollary 1, manuscript p.31
notes: The factorization for (C,TF) is essential.

statement: $T\widetilde C:=\widetilde C\cap W$, with $TC\subset T\widetilde C$.
notes: Equations (5.3)--(5.4).

statement: Every $f\in\widetilde C\cap W$ is a retract, with its source fixed, of an arrow in $TC$.
gap_or_error: The proof and diagram write f∈C rather than f∈tilde C.
repair: The intended hypothesis f∈tilde C gives precisely the needed lift against p∈TF. Two-out-of-three puts the left factor in TC, and the section exhibits the retract.

statement: Every right lifting class Ψ is closed under small products of maps, including the empty product. Consequently the preceding product formula makes u_* preserve objectwise Ψ maps.
notes: Proof of6.4(c). For a square against a product of right-class maps, solve each projected square and combine the lifts; choice is used for a general family. The last source sentence writes u_* where u_*(X) is intended.
